searchText: Why do we have "evm" and "evm-graveyard" channels? I think evm-graveyard was created specifically to talk about potentially backwards compatibility breaking simplifications to the ethereum environment See the pinned message. I remember the intend, but nowadays seems content is the same on both. We should probably do better at redirecting people to the right channel, or merge them if there is too little content to warrant two channels. My problem with charging for extending memory (<@194433073394352129> 's concern too https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3336) is that RAM is addressed in pages, and CPU cache in lines, and writing to an address touches only that line and page, not the intervening ones. How expensive that is depends on lots of things that we probably should consider more than we have -- see [What Every Programmer Should Know About Memory](https://people.freebsd.org/~lstewart/articles/cpumemory.pdf) (A cost model that charges for extension encourages programs to use to use MSIZE to mark the next free address, but they can do that no matter the cost model.)
